collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DISABILITY AND HUMAN DIVERSITY (DIV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Disabled villagers, chronic illness and every kind of body, skin, hair and face: wheelchairs with real wheels, crutches, canes, ear trumpets, signs and lenses made from island materials; good days and hard days; competence, humor and opinions. Sometimes the difference is the story. Often it's just part of the scenery.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager grabs a blind villager's arm to steer them, unasked: say so plainly, or make a joke of it.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) is blind and walking to the meeting hut, the way (subject.he/she) does every day, when (friend) rushes up, grabs (subject.his/her) arm and starts steering (subject.him/her) across the clearing, chattering kindly. (subject) didn't need help and doesn't like being grabbed. (subject.He/she) stops walking.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "Please let go," says (subject). (friend) lets go at once, startled. "If you want to help, ask first. If I say yes, I'll take your arm. Not the other way round." (friend) is embarrassed, and a bit hurt, and then thinks about it. "Do you want help?" (friend.he/she) asks. "Not today," says (subject). "But thank you for asking." (subject.He/she) walks off, perfectly straight, to the meeting hut.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "Where are we going?" asks (subject). "The meeting hut!" says (friend). "I know. I was already going there. Before I was kidnapped." (friend) lets go, mortified. (subject) laughs. "Ask next time. I might even say yes." Next time, (friend) asks. (subject) says no, cheerfully, and they walk there side by side anyway.
